components.note: 疒 (illness, 病字旁) — illness and pain: 病 ill, 疼 ache, 瘦 thin, 疯 mad; 痛 is pain.
甬 (yǒng) is a loose sound clue; same part in 通 tōng and 桶 tǒng.
艹 (grass, plants) — plants and herbs: 花 flower, 草 grass, 茶 tea; 苦 first named a bitter herb.
古 (gǔ) is a loose clue for kǔ — see also 枯 kū and 姑 gū.

example.hanzi: 失去亲人的痛苦很难忘记。
example.pinyin: Shīqù qīnrén de tòngkǔ hěn nán wàngjì.
example.english: The pain of losing a loved one is hard to forget.
example.fact: 痛苦 doubles up two characters that are each already painful on their own — 痛 (“physical pain, ache”) and 苦 (“bitter, suffering”) — fusing a bodily sense with a tasting/emotional one into a single word that spans both physical and emotional suffering.

examples.pinyin: Shēngbìng hěn tòngkǔ.
examples.english: Being sick is painful.

examples.hanzi: 他脸上露出了痛苦的表情。
examples.pinyin: Tā liǎn shàng lùchūle tòngkǔ de biǎoqíng.
examples.english: A pained expression appeared on his face.

components.note: 玉 (jade) — jade put away safely: 全 first meant flawless, pure, then whole.
阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 那: a district or ministry.
咅 (pǒu) is a loose sound clue for bù; 咅 also in 剖 pōu, 培 péi and 陪 péi.

example.pinyin: Zhèxiē shū quánbù dōu shì wǒ de.
example.english: All of these books are mine.
example.fact: 全部 behaves as a noun for “the whole, the entirety” and often takes 都 afterward for emphasis (全部都...) — unlike 所有, which sits directly in front of a noun (所有的书, “all the books”), 全部 more often stands alone or trails the noun it refers back to.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ qián quánbù huāwán le.
examples.english: I've spent all the money.

examples.pinyin: Quánbù de rén dōu dào le.
examples.english: Everyone has arrived.

components.note: 手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.

example.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ shǒujī fàng zài bāo lǐ le.
example.english: I put my phone in my bag.
example.fact: 手机 is literally “hand machine” (手 “hand” + 机 “machine”) — a plainly descriptive coinage for the mobile phone, the same instinct behind English “cell phone” and “mobile phone” rather than a borrowed or invented term.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de shǒujī xiǎng le.
examples.english: Your phone is ringing.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yí bù xīn shǒujī.
examples.english: I want to buy a new phone.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and thinking: 想 think, 思, 感 feel, 忙; forgetting is a loss of the heart's hold.
亡 (wáng, lose) gives the sound and fits the sense: to lose from the mind.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 记 is to note down or remember.
己 (jǐ) is a close sound clue for jì; 己 also sounds out 纪 jì and 起 qǐ.

example.pinyin: Bié wàngjì dài sǎn.
example.english: Don't forget to bring an umbrella.
example.fact: 忘记 fuses 忘 (“to forget”) with its near-opposite 记 (“to remember, record”) into a single word meaning “to forget” — Chinese has a handful of compounds built the same way from an antonym pair, the best-known being 呼吸 (“to breathe,” from 呼 “to exhale” + 吸 “to inhale”).

examples.hanzi: 我忘记了他的电话号码。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ wàngjìle tā de diànhuà hàomǎ.
examples.english: I forgot his phone number.

examples.pinyin: Bú yào wàngjì chī yào.
examples.english: Don't forget to take your medicine.

components.note: 子 (child) — children and offspring: 孩 child, 学 study, 孙 grandchild; 存 means to keep or survive.
才 (cái) is only a loose sound hint for cún.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地 earth, 坐 sit; 在 is "to be at a place".
才 (cái) is a close sound clue for zài; 才 also appears in 材 cái.

example.pinyin: Zhège wèntí yìzhí cúnzài.
example.english: This problem has always existed.
example.fact: 存在 combines 存 (“to survive, preserve”) and 在 (“to be present, at”), two characters that can each independently gesture at “existing” — reinforcing two near-synonyms into one word is the same strategy behind common words like 喜欢 (“to like,” from “joy” + “joy”) and 应该 (“should,” from two words each meaning roughly “ought to”).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiāngxìn wàixīngrén cúnzài.
examples.english: I believe aliens exist.

examples.hanzi: 这家商店已经不存在了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā shāngdiàn yǐjīng bù cúnzài le.
examples.english: This shop no longer exists.

components.note: 首 (head, first) — a picture of a head with hair on top, which became the word for first and chief: 首先, 元首, also a measure for songs.
儿 (legs, person) — with a foot 𠂉 above: a foot stepping out in front of a person, so "first, earlier".

example.hanzi: 首先,我要感谢大家的支持。
example.pinyin: Shǒuxiān, wǒ yào gǎnxiè dàjiā de zhīchí.
example.english: First of all, I want to thank everyone for their support.
example.fact: 首先 is a formal opener for listing points (首先...然后...最后..., “first...then...finally...”) fitting written or public-speaking contexts — in casual conversation, speakers often just say plain 先 instead, saving 首先 for more structured moments.

examples.pinyin: Shǒuxiān, qǐng dàjiā ānjìng.
examples.english: First of all, everyone please be quiet.

examples.pinyin: Zuòfàn shí, shǒuxiān yào xǐ cài.
examples.english: When cooking, you first need to wash the vegetables.

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 给, 线; 组 is to weave threads together, so to form a group.
且 (qiě) loosely hints at zǔ; 组 sounds exactly like 祖 zǔ and 阻 zǔ, same part.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen shì yí gè xiǎozǔ.
example.english: We are a small group.
example.fact: 组 is to form and a group: 小组 (team), 组织 (organise), 组成 (be made up of), 组合 (combination). In Chinese schools, a 小组 is a study group.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiǎozǔ yǒu wǔ ge rén.
examples.english: Our group has five people.

examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī bǎ xuésheng fēnchéng sān zǔ.
examples.english: The teacher divided the students into three groups.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — fire and heat, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 黑 black: light shining.
昭 (zhāo) is a close sound clue for zhào; 昭 itself means bright.

example.pinyin: Qǐng zhào zhège fāngfǎ zuò.
example.english: Please do it according to this method.
example.fact: 照 means to shine, to take a photo (照相) and 'according to' (照着). 照片 is a photo, 照顾 means to look after and 护照 is a passport.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ gěi wǒmen zhào zhāng xiàng.
examples.english: Please take a photo of us.

examples.pinyin: Yángguāng zhào zài wǒ de liǎn shang.
examples.english: The sunlight shines on my face.

components.note: 交 (cross, hand over) — a person with legs crossed: to intersect, then to exchange. Same part in 校 xiào, 较 jiào, 胶 jiāo.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zuòyè jiāo gěi lǎoshī.
example.english: Please hand in your homework to the teacher.
example.fact: 交 means to hand over, to cross and to make friends: 交作业, 交钱 (pay), 交朋友 and 交通 (traffic). 交 is a classic action word for 'hand in' tasks.

examples.pinyin: Tā hěn huì jiāo péngyou.
examples.english: He is good at making friends.

examples.pinyin: Míngtiān yào jiāo zuòyè le.
examples.english: The homework is due tomorrow.

components.note: 人 (person) — the right-hand part. The left part is a hook-and-dot, from an old tool-like shape. Meaning 'by means of, so as to' is not shown by the parts today.
Memory aid: a person 人 using a tool to get something done — 'by means of' (可以, 所以, 以前). A mnemonic, not proven etymology.
及 (reach) — a hand 又 catching up with a person from behind: to reach, then and; seen in 以及, 及时.

example.hanzi: 会议邀请了老师、学生以及家长。
example.pinyin: Huìyì yāoqǐng le lǎoshī, xuésheng yǐjí jiāzhǎng.
example.english: The meeting invited teachers, students, as well as parents.
example.fact: 以及 is generally reserved for the last, often somewhat distinct item in a list, especially in formal writing, while 和 or 跟 handle everyday “and” between ordinary items — reaching for 以及 signals a small shift in kind or importance for what follows.

examples.pinyin: Zhuō shàng yǒu píngguǒ yǐjí xiāngjiāo.
examples.english: There are apples as well as bananas on the table.

examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan yīnyuè yǐjí yùndòng.
examples.english: He likes music and sports.

components.note: 十 (ten) — a cross: first a single vertical line, later crossed with a horizontal bar. Seen in 十分, 二十, and in 千.

example.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu shí gè píngguǒ.
example.english: I have ten apples.
example.fact: 十 is a simple cross and also stands for 'complete' in idioms: 十全十美 means 'perfect in every way'. For tens, 十一 is 11, and 二十 is 20.

examples.pinyin: Xiànzài shì shí diǎn.
examples.english: It's ten o'clock now.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bān yǒu sìshí ge xuésheng.
examples.english: There are forty students in our class.

components.note: 台 (tái) as a sound part appears in 抬 tái, 胎 tāi, 苔 tái, and also in 治 zhì and 始 shǐ.

example.pinyin: Tā zǒushàngle wǔtái.
example.english: He walked onto the stage.
example.fact: 台 is a platform or stage, as in 舞台, 电视台 (TV station) and 台风 (typhoon). It's also the measure word for machines and shows (一台电脑) and the short name for Taiwan (台湾).

examples.pinyin: Zhuō shang yǒu yì tái diànnǎo.
examples.english: There's a computer on the desk.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ qù qiántái wèn yíxià.
examples.english: You can ask at the front desk.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 拿, 提, 抬; 搬 is to move things.
般 (bān) gives the sound exactly: 搬 bān.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān bānjiā.
example.english: We are moving house tomorrow.
example.fact: 搬 means to move bulky things from one place to another: 搬家 (move house), 搬东西 (carry things) and 搬运 (transport). It's used for moving objects, whereas 移 is more abstract.

examples.hanzi: 你能帮我搬这个箱子吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng bāng wǒ bān zhège xiāngzi ma?
examples.english: Can you help me move this box?

examples.hanzi: 他们上个月搬到了新家。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen shàng ge yuè bāndàole xīn jiā.
examples.english: They moved into a new home last month.

components.note: 人 (person) — the top part. 个 is the general measure word, as in 一个, 这个, 那个.
丨 (a vertical tally) — under 人, read as one tally mark per person: counting individuals one by one.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ gèrén de kànfǎ.
example.english: This is my personal opinion.
example.fact: 个人 sits directly in front of a noun to mean “personal, individual” (个人看法, 个人信息) without any adjective-forming suffix the way English needs “-al” to turn “person” into “personal” — the noun itself does double duty.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng yào yí ge gèrén fángjiān.
examples.english: I'd like a private room.

examples.pinyin: Gèrén de nǔlì hěn zhòngyào.
examples.english: Individual effort is important.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and roles: 你, 他, 位; 代 is one person replacing another, then a generation.
弋 (yì) is only a loose hint; 代 itself sounds out 袋 dài and 贷 dài.
衣 (clothes; 衤 on the left) — the outer garment.
毛 (fur) — a fur coat worn outside: the outside, the surface, then to show.

example.hanzi: 他代表公司参加了会议。
example.pinyin: Tā dàibiǎo gōngsī cānjiā le huìyì.
example.english: He represented the company at the meeting.
example.fact: 代表 splits cleanly along its two characters' older senses: 代 (“to take the place of, substitute”) and 表 (“to express, show”) — together, roughly “to stand in for and express on behalf of,” a fairly transparent path to the modern meanings “to represent” and “representative.”

examples.pinyin: Tā shì xuésheng de dàibiǎo.
examples.english: She is the students' representative.

examples.pinyin: Hóngsè dàibiǎo hǎoyùn.
examples.english: Red represents good luck.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and land: 地, 场, 城; hard like packed earth. Top part simplifies 臤 (hard), also in 紧 jǐn and 贤 xián.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: holding on.
寺 (sì) is a loose sound clue for chí; 寺 also in 诗 shī, 待 dài, 特 tè and 等 děng.

example.hanzi: 只要坚持下去,你就会成功。
example.pinyin: Zhǐyào jiānchí xiàqù, nǐ jiù huì chénggōng.
example.english: As long as you keep persisting, you will succeed.
example.fact: 坚持 very often takes the directional complement 下去 (“to continue on,” literally “go down”) right after it — 坚持下去 (“to keep persisting”) is one of the most common fixed collocations built around this word.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào jiānchí duànliàn shēntǐ.
examples.english: We must keep exercising.

examples.pinyin: Tā jiānchí zìjǐ de kànfǎ.
examples.english: He sticks to his own view.

components.note: 心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.
义 (justice, meaning) also lends its sound to 议 yì discuss, 仪 yí ceremony and 蚁 yǐ ant — a useful clue in many characters.

example.hanzi: 这次旅行对我很有意义。
example.pinyin: Zhècì lǚxíng duì wǒ hěn yǒu yìyì.
example.english: This trip was very meaningful to me.
example.fact: 意义 is almost always framed with 有 for “meaningful” (有意义) and 没有 for “meaningless” (没有意义) — since the word itself is a noun, Chinese needs this 有/没有 wrapper to do the job English gets straight from the adjective “meaningful.”

examples.pinyin: Zhège cí yǒu shénme yìyì?
examples.english: What's the meaning of this word?

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì yìyì hěn dà.
examples.english: This matter is of great significance.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 木 is wood and trees, as in 树, 板, 桌; buildings with floors were built of wood, hence 楼.
娄 (lóu) — same sound — 楼 is lóu; 娄 also sounds out 搂 lǒu.

example.pinyin: Wǒ zhù zài sān lóu.
example.english: I live on the third floor.
example.fact: 楼 is a multi-storey building and a floor number: 五楼 (5th floor), 楼上 (upstairs), 楼梯 (staircase) and 大楼 (building). In Chinese, ground floor is 一楼, as in American usage.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò lóu yǒu èrshí céng.
examples.english: This building has twenty floors.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài lóuxià děng nǐ.
examples.english: He is waiting for you downstairs.

components.note: 手 (hand) — the hand family: 打, 拿, 拉. 承 is usually explained as hands lifting something, to bear or accept (承认 admit, 承诺 promise).
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; recognising something is naming it.
人 (rén) gives the exact sound, and also means "person".

example.hanzi: 他终于承认了自己的错误。
example.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú chéngrèn le zìjǐ de cuòwù.
example.english: He finally admitted his mistake.
example.fact: 承认 covers both “to admit” (a fault) and “to recognize” (a government, a diploma, a fact) in diplomatic and legal registers, as in 承认一个国家 (“to recognize a country”) — one word spanning what English splits into “admit” and “recognize.”

examples.pinyin: Wǒ chéngrèn wǒ cuò le.
examples.english: I admit I was wrong.

examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu chéngrèn tā de nénglì.
examples.english: Everyone recognizes his ability.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
言 (speech) — the traditional form of 讠: words and speech; an oath is a spoken promise.
折 (zhé, to break) — a promise you must not break; zhé is only a loose sound hint for shì.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiàng nǐ fāshì, zhè shì zhēn de.
example.english: I swear to you, this is true.
example.fact: 发誓 is literally “to issue an oath” (发 “to issue, send out” + 誓 “oath, vow”) — the same productive 发 turns up in 发言 (“to speak up”) and 发信 (“to send a letter”), all sharing the sense of something being released or put forth.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ fāshì bú huì gàosu biérén.
examples.english: I swear I won't tell anyone.

examples.pinyin: Tā fāshì yào jièyān.
examples.english: He vowed to quit smoking.

components.note: 王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.
由 (from, reason) — mostly useful as a sound part: 油 yóu, 邮 yóu, 柚 yòu, 抽 chōu all contain it.

example.pinyin: Nǐ méiyǒu lǐyóu shēngqì.
example.english: You have no reason to be angry.
example.fact: 理由 and 原因 both translate as “reason,” but 理由 leans toward a justification someone offers for a choice, while 原因 leans toward the objective cause of an event — 没有理由 (“no justification”) reads differently from 没有原因 (“no cause”).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu shénme lǐyóu chídào?
examples.english: What's your reason for being late?

examples.pinyin: Tā de lǐyóu hěn jiǎndān.
examples.english: His reason is very simple.

components.note: 日 (sun) — light and brightness: 明, 晴, 时; 显 is something lit up and clear to see.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 照 shine. 然 first meant "to burn" (燃 rán adds 火 later); "so, naturally" is borrowed.
肰 (rán) gives the exact sound and shows up in 燃 rán.

example.pinyin: Xiǎnrán, tā méiyǒu zuò hǎo zhǔnbèi.
example.english: Clearly, he wasn't well prepared.
example.fact: 显然 typically opens a sentence as a stand-alone adverb commenting on the whole clause that follows, much like English “clearly” or “obviously” at a sentence's start — a common marker for a speaker's confident inference, in both writing and speech.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎnrán tā hěn bù gāoxìng.
examples.english: Obviously he's very unhappy.

examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí xiǎnrán hěn nán.
examples.english: This question is clearly hard.

components.note: 尺 (ruler) — the main part, as in 尺寸 size. Dictionary story: a place where measures are discussed (口), like a bureau; 局 also means 'game' as in 结局.
口 (mouth/box) — placed inside 尺. It represents talk or a space; Memory aid: a ruler fitted to a mouth means rules are discussed in an 'office'.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen xiàle yì jú qí.
example.english: We played a game of chess.
example.fact: 局 is a bureau or office (邮局, post office; 公安局, police station), a situation (局面) and a measure word for a round of a game (一局棋). 结局 means 'ending' of a story.

examples.pinyin: Bǐsài dì yī jú tā yíng le.
examples.english: He won the first round of the match.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài yóujú jìle yì fēng xìn.
examples.english: He mailed a letter at the post office.

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — acts that direct others: 教 teach, 放 release, 改 change, 收 collect; 政 is governing.
正 (zhèng) is the same sound; fits the sense too — government puts things right.
广 (building, shelter) — houses and large structures: 店 shop, 库 store, 度, 座; 府 is an official residence.
付 (fù) is close to fǔ; also 附 fù and 符 fú.

example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ xuānbù le xīn de zhèngcè.
example.english: The government announced a new policy.
example.fact: 政府 combines 政 (“governance, politics”) with 府 (“official residence, mansion”) — 府 alone also names a seat of administration in words like 首府 (“provincial capital”), reflecting an older habit of naming a ruling body after the building that housed it.

examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ zhèngzài jiàn xīn xuéxiào.
examples.english: The government is building a new school.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài zhèngfǔ gōngzuò.
examples.english: He works for the government.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and place, as in 道 way, 过 pass, 近 near; the radical hints at "here / this way". The 文 part is not a useful sound clue.
欠 (open mouth, lack) — yawning, breathing and wanting: 歌 song, 欢 joy, 吹 blow; 次 also sounds out 资 zī and 瓷 cí.

example.pinyin: Zhècì kǎoshì hěn nán.
example.english: This exam was very difficult.
example.fact: 次 is Mandarin's general measure word for counting discrete occurrences (一次, 两次, 这次) — the counterpart to 个 as the default measure word for objects, which makes 这次 (“this occurrence, this time”) the event-counting twin of 这个 (“this one”).

examples.pinyin: Zhè cì wǒ qǐngkè.
examples.english: It's my treat this time.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhè cì qù nǎr lǚxíng?
examples.english: Where are you traveling this time?

components.note: 土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.

example.hanzi: 他在这里做生意已经十年了。
example.pinyin: Tā zài zhèlǐ zuò shēngyi yǐjīng shí nián le.
example.english: He has been doing business here for ten years.
example.fact: 生意 has two separate CEDICT entries sharing the same characters but differing in tone: everyday shēngyi, with a neutral second syllable, means “business, trade” and explains this word's high frequency, while the fully-toned shēngyì is a rarer, more literary word for “life force, vitality” — the same characters, a different register and reading entirely.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàba zuò shēngyi.
examples.english: My dad is in business.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de shēngyi hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This shop does great business.

components.note: 目 (eye) — sight, as in 看, 睛, 睡.
艮 (gèn) is a loose sound clue for yǎn; 艮 also sounds out 跟 gēn, 很 hěn and 根 gēn.

example.pinyin: Tā de yǎnjing hěn dà.
example.english: His eyes are big.
example.fact: 眼 is the eye, usually as 眼睛; it also counts glances (看一眼 'take a look') and small holes (泉眼). 眼 appears in 眼镜 (glasses) and 眼泪 (tears).

examples.pinyin: Tā de yǎnjing yòu dà yòu liàng.
examples.english: Her eyes are big and bright.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bìshàng yǎn, shǔdào shí.
examples.english: Please close your eyes and count to ten.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过 pass, 进 enter, 送 send; to meet is to cross paths.
禺 (yú) is close to yù; same part in 愚 yú and 偶 ǒu.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.hanzi: 我在路上遇到了一个老朋友。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zài lùshang yùdào le yí gè lǎo péngyou.
example.english: I ran into an old friend on the road.
example.fact: 遇到 pairs 遇 (“to encounter”) with the same success-marking 到 also seen in 做到 (rank 452 in this batch) and the common verb 看到 (“to see, to succeed in seeing”) — the compound stresses that the encounter actually happened, rather than merely being attempted or hoped for.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yùdàole yí ge nántí.
examples.english: I ran into a difficult problem.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yùdào shénme máfan le ma?
examples.english: Did you run into any trouble?

components.note: 火 (fire) — a picture of flames, and a component seen in 烧, 灯, 热 (as the dots 灬), 炒; fire radical for burning and heat.

example.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn huǒ!
example.english: Watch out for the fire!
example.fact: 火 is fire and also 'popular': 火车 (train, literally 'fire cart'), 火山 (volcano), 生火 (light a fire). In slang, 火 means 'hot, trendy', as in 这首歌很火. In Chinese medicine, 上火 is 'too much internal heat'.

examples.pinyin: Shuǐ tài tàng, huǒ yào guānxiǎo yìdiǎn.
examples.english: The water is too hot, turn the flame down.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuò huǒchē qù Shànghǎi.
examples.english: I'm taking the train to Shanghai.

components.note: 犭 (animal; 犬 dog) — marks animals, as in 狗 dog, 猪 pig, 狼 wolf; 猫 is the cat.
苗 (miáo) — close sound: 猫 māo, like a cat's meow; 苗 also sounds out 描 miáo.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu yì zhī māo.
example.english: My family has a cat.
example.fact: 猫 takes the measure word 只 (一只猫). It forms 熊猫 (panda, literally 'bear cat'), 小猫 (kitten) and 猫咪 (kitty, cute). The phrase 招财猫 is the lucky waving cat.

examples.pinyin: Nà zhī māo zài shài tàiyang.
examples.english: That cat is sunbathing.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ mèimei xǐhuan xiǎomāo.
examples.english: My younger sister likes kittens.

components.note: 卩 (kneeling person) — a person kneeling at food 皀, about to eat: right at hand, immediately; compare 既, who has already eaten.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and roles: 你, 他, 位; 使 is sending someone to do something.
吏 (lì, official) gives the meaning, and shares its ancestor 史 (shǐ), the exact sound of 使.

example.pinyin: Jíshǐ xiàyǔ, wǒmen yě huì qù.
example.english: Even if it rains, we'll still go.
example.fact: 即使 is almost always paired with 也 in the clause that follows (即使...,也...), the same two-part frame that 虽然 forms with 但是 — Chinese marks both halves of the sentence where English's single “even if” only needs to appear once.

examples.hanzi: 即使很累,他也坚持工作。
examples.pinyin: Jíshǐ hěn lèi, tā yě jiānchí gōngzuò.
examples.english: Even if he's tired, he keeps working.

examples.pinyin: Jíshǐ nǐ bù shuō, wǒ yě zhīdào.
examples.english: Even if you don't say it, I know.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 记 is to note down or remember.
己 (jǐ) is a close sound clue for jì; 己 also sounds out 纪 jì and 起 qǐ.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; also in 注 zhù and 柱 zhù, and 主 means master (a person who stays).

example.pinyin: Qǐng jìzhu wǒ de míngzi.
example.english: Please remember my name.
example.fact: 记住 pairs 记 (“to record, remember”) with the resultative complement 住 (“to hold firmly, to stay”) — 住 here doesn't mean “to live” but marks that the remembering “sticks,” the same job it does in 抓住 (“to grab hold of”) and 站住 (“to stand firm”).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào jìzhu zhège mìmǎ.
examples.english: You need to remember this password.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ méiyǒu jìzhu tā de míngzi.
examples.english: I didn't remember his name.

components.note: 至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.
夂 (foot) — stopping or going: 处 first meant to stay or settle, then a place or to deal with.

example.pinyin: Tā dàochù zhǎo tā de qiánbāo.
example.english: He looked everywhere for his wallet.
example.fact: 到处 is literally “to every place” (到 “to reach, arrive” + 处 “place, location”) and works as an adverb sitting directly before the verb it modifies (到处找, “to search everywhere”), unlike English “everywhere,” which can also trail after the verb or a preposition.

examples.pinyin: Jiālǐ dàochù dōu shì wánjù.
examples.english: There are toys everywhere at home.

examples.pinyin: Dàochù dōu shì rén.
examples.english: There are people everywhere.

components.note: 幸 (luck) — often read as an old picture of shackles; 'luck' is escaping punishment. The dictionary story (one alive 土, one dead 干) is a memory aid.
土 (earth) — the top. Memory aid: the one standing on solid ground 土 is the lucky one — 幸运, 幸福.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 运 is to move, then to be moved by luck.
云 (yún) is a near sound match for yùn.

example.pinyin: Wǒ juéde zìjǐ hěn xìngyùn.
example.english: I feel very lucky.
example.fact: 幸运 works as both an adjective (“lucky”) and a noun (“good fortune, luck”), so 很幸运 (“very lucky”) and 是我的幸运 (“is my good fortune”) both use the same word unchanged — another case in this list of a word crossing freely between adjective and noun.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhēn xìngyùn!
examples.english: You're so lucky!

examples.hanzi: 他很幸运地找到了工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn xìngyùn de zhǎodàole gōngzuò.
examples.english: He luckily found a job.

components.note: 上 (above) — 上 over 下 squeezed together: something stuck in the middle, the sense of qiǎ (to wedge); kǎ is the borrowed sound for "card" and "car", as in 信用卡 and 卡车.

example.pinyin: Wǒ méi dài yínháng kǎ.
example.english: I didn't bring my bank card.
example.fact: 卡 is borrowed from English 'card' as in 银行卡, 信用卡 and 卡片. It's also used for 'to be stuck': 卡住 (get stuck), and in slang 很卡 means a laggy device. Sometimes it's read qiǎ (to block), as in 关卡.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu xìnyòngkǎ ma?
examples.english: Do you have a credit card?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī yǒudiǎn kǎ.
examples.english: My phone is a bit laggy.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 洗 is to wash.
先 (xiān) — near sound — 洗 is xǐ; 先 also sounds out 选 xuǎn.

example.pinyin: Wǒ yào xǐ shǒu.
example.english: I need to wash my hands.
example.fact: 洗 is to wash: 洗手, 洗脸, 洗澡 (bathe), 洗衣服, 洗碗 (wash dishes). It also appears in 洗手间 (restroom) and 洗发水 (shampoo).

examples.pinyin: Chīfàn qián xiān xǐshǒu.
examples.english: Wash your hands before eating.

examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ yào xǐ yīfu.
examples.english: I need to do laundry this weekend.

components.note: 阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 部 part. 那 was a place name before it meant "that".
日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.pinyin: Nàshí wǒmen hái hěn niánqīng.
example.english: At that time, we were still very young.
example.fact: 那时 pairs the far demonstrative 那 (“that”) with 时 (“time”), mirroring how 这时 (“at this time, right now”) is built — the same far/near split behind 那个/这个 and 那么/这么 carries over consistently into this pair as well.

examples.pinyin: Nàshí wǒ hái zài shàng xiǎoxué.
examples.english: I was still in elementary school then.

examples.pinyin: Nà shí de tiānqì bǐ xiànzài lěng.
examples.english: The weather then was colder than now.

components.note: 干 (dry; do) — a forked pole or shield. It lends its sound to 肝 gān, 杆 gān, 赶 gǎn, 汗 hàn and 岸 àn.
十 (shí, ten) is a loose sound clue for 什 (shén, shí in 什锦); old sense "a set of ten", hence "assorted". In 什么 it is simply "what".
幺 (tiny, a thread) — 么 looks like 幺 and was borrowed as a simplified form for the light particle in 什么, 怎么, 这么. The shape does not explain the meaning today.
厶 (loop) — the visible lower part, a small curl. Memory aid: a tiny stroke 丿 over a curl — a 'little something' you ask about: 什么 what?

example.pinyin: Nǐ zài zhèr gànshénme?
example.english: What are you doing here?
example.fact: 干什么 is the blunter, more colloquial cousin of 做什么 — 干 as a verb for “to do” carries a rougher, more casual edge than the neutral 做, so depending on tone of voice 干什么 can land as impatient or accusatory in a way the flat English translation “what are you doing” doesn't capture.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ gàn shénme qù?
examples.english: Where are you off to?

examples.pinyin: Bié gàn shénme dōu màntūntūn de.
examples.english: Don't be slow at everything you do.

meanings: matter that needs to be settled

components.note: 彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.
儿 (child, legs) — shows a person's legs; in 兒 the top was a child's soft skull. As an ending (这儿) it adds the er sound; 儿 also in 先, 兄, 光.

example.pinyin: Nǐ jīntiān yǒu shìr ma?
example.english: Do you have something on today?
example.fact: The 儿 in 事儿 is a Beijing-rooted retroflex ending (erhua) that fuses into the previous syllable's pronunciation rather than forming its own syllable — 事儿 is pronounced as one syllable, “shir,” not two.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒudiǎn shìr yào zhǎo nǐ.
examples.english: I have something to talk to you about.

examples.pinyin: Méi shìr, bié dānxīn.
examples.english: It's nothing, don't worry.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and mixing liquids, as in 河, 海, 清: 混 is to mix or muddy.
昆 (kūn) is a close sound clue for hùn; 昆 also in 棍 gùn.

example.pinyin: Tā zài gōngsī hùnle jǐ nián.
example.english: He kicked around the company for a few years.
example.fact: 混 is to mix, and in speech it can also mean to muddle through or hang around: 混日子 (idle away time), 混饭吃 (just get by). 混 is read hún in 混蛋 (scoundrel) and in the sense of 'muddy'.

examples.pinyin: Shuǐ hé yóu hùn bu dào yìqǐ.
examples.english: Water and oil don't mix.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài dà chéngshì hùnle shí nián.
examples.english: He scraped by in a big city for ten years.

components.note: 犭 (beast, form of 犬 dog) — animals: 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狼 wolf; 犯 is to attack or violate, hence offend.
罒 (net, form of 网) — nets and entrapment: 罗 net, 罚 punish, 骂 scold; here a net of wrongdoing 非 catching the guilty.
非 (not, wrong) — what is wrong or unlawful; in 罪 it is the wrongdoing caught in the net.

example.hanzi: 他因为犯罪被送进了监狱。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi fànzuì bèi sòng jìn le jiānyù.
example.english: He was sent to prison because he committed a crime.
example.fact: 犯罪 combines 犯 (“to violate, offend”) with 罪 (“crime, sin”) — the same productive 犯 shows up in 犯错 (“to make a mistake”) and 犯法 (“to break the law”), a recurring verb for “to commit/violate” across different kinds of wrongdoing.

examples.pinyin: Fànzuì shì bú duì de.
examples.english: Committing a crime is wrong.

examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zài yùfáng fànzuì.
examples.english: The police are working to prevent crime.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 拉 pull, 提 lift; 挂 is hanging something up.
圭 (guī) — close sound: 挂 guà. 圭 also sounds out 鞋 xié and 娃 wá.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ yīfu guà qǐlai.
example.english: Please hang up the clothes.
example.fact: 挂 is to hang or to hang up (the phone): 挂电话, 挂号 (register at a hospital), 挂念 (to be concerned). In modern slang 挂了 can mean 'it's dead / crashed' or 'he died'.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng guàhǎo nǐ de wàitào.
examples.english: Please hang up your coat.

examples.pinyin: Tā shēngqì de guàle diànhuà.
examples.english: He angrily hung up the phone.

components.note: ⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and walking: 跑 run, 踢 kick, 路 road, 跟 follow; 跳 is a jump.
兆 (zhào) is a loose hint; the series 桃 táo, 逃 táo, 挑 tiāo, 眺 tiào shares the -ao sound.
舛 (two opposed feet) — the dancer's footwork; 無 (wú) above is a loose sound clue, as it once meant dance itself.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò jīngcháng qù tiàowǔ.
example.english: We often go dancing on weekends.
example.fact: 跳舞 is a verb-object compound, literally “to jump a dance” (跳 “to jump, leap” + 舞 “dance”) — like other activity verbs of this shape, such as 唱歌 (“to sing a song”) and 游泳 (“to swim a swim”), the “object” half can even be separated out (跳了一支舞, “danced a dance”) despite 跳舞 feeling like one fused verb.

examples.pinyin: Tā cóng xiǎo jiù ài tiàowǔ.
examples.english: She has loved dancing since she was little.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ huì tiàowǔ ma?
examples.english: Can you dance?

components.note: 白 (white, bright) — gives sound to 拍 pāi, 怕 pà, 伯 bó and 泊 bó. Meaning: white, clear, plain, hence "明白" understand.
疒 (illness, 病字旁) — illness: 病, 疼, 瘦; 痴 is a sickness of the mind, hence foolish or obsessed.
知 (zhī) is a loose sound hint for chī.

example.hanzi: 别再犯这种白痴的错误了。
example.pinyin: Bié zài fàn zhè zhǒng báichī de cuòwù le.
example.english: Don't make such idiotic mistakes again.
example.fact: 白 here likely contributes the sense of "blank" (an empty mind), while 痴 alone recurs across a family of words for foolish infatuation — 痴迷 ("besotted"), 情痴 ("lovesick fool") — all sharing the illness radical 疒 that frames obsession as a kind of sickness of the mind.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme néng zhème báichī?
examples.english: How can you be such an idiot?

examples.hanzi: 电影里的白痴角色把大家都逗笑了。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de báichī juésè bǎ dàjiā dōu dòuxiào le.
examples.english: The idiot character in the movie made everyone laugh.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person and his word: 言 (speech) beside it gives a person who keeps his word, hence "trust, believe".
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters, as in 说, 请, 谢.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做; 任 is a duty a person bears.
壬 (rén) gives the same sound, different tone; also in 妊 rèn.

example.hanzi: 我们之间需要更多的信任。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhījiān xūyào gèng duō de xìnrèn.
example.english: We need more trust between us.
example.fact: 信任 describes trusting a person or institution as reliable over time (信任朋友, "trust a friend"), while 相信 is used for believing a specific statement or fact (相信他的话, "believe what he says") — two different English senses of "trust/believe" that Chinese keeps grammatically distinct.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xìnrèn wǒ de péngyou.
examples.english: I trust my friend a lot.

examples.pinyin: Tā bù xìnrèn mòshēngrén.
examples.english: He doesn't trust strangers.

components.note: 斤 (axe) — chopping, as in 所, 斩: freshly cut wood is new (薪 xīn is firewood).
亲 (qīn) is a close sound clue for xīn.
耳 (ear) — hearing: 听 listen, 聋 deaf, 聪 clever; 闻 is to hear, then news.
门 (mén) is a near sound match (wén); also in 问 wèn ask.

example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang kàn xīnwén.
example.english: I watch the news every morning.
example.fact: 闻 originally meant simply "to hear" (its ear radical 耳 still shows this) before narrowing to "smell" in isolation and broadening to "news" in compounds — so 新闻, literally "newly heard [things]", preserves the character's oldest sense better than most modern uses of 闻 alone.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kàn jīntiān de xīnwén le ma?
examples.english: Did you watch today's news?

examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xīnwén shì zhēn de ma?
examples.english: Is this news item true?

components.note: 未 (not yet) — a tree 木 with a new short branch on top, still growing. Compare 末 mò (end/tip), where the top stroke is longer.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.hanzi: 谁也不知道未来会怎样。
example.pinyin: Shéi yě bù zhīdào wèilái huì zěnyàng.
example.english: No one knows what the future will be like.
example.fact: 未来 is built from two transparent time-logic characters: 未 ("not yet") plus 来 ("to come") literally spells out "not-yet-arrived" — the same 未 shows up in 未婚 ("not yet married") and 未成年 ("not yet an adult, i.e. a minor").

examples.pinyin: Wèilái de shēnghuó huì gèng fāngbiàn.
examples.english: Life in the future will be more convenient.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ duì wèilái yǒu shénme dǎsuan?
examples.english: What are your plans for the future?

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.
欠 (lack, yawn) — open mouth or something missing, as in 次 and 欢; 歉 is feeling short, hence sorry.
兼 (jiān) is a loose sound clue for qiàn; 兼 also sounds out 嫌 xián and 谦 qiān.

example.pinyin: Tā xiàng wǒ dàoqiàn le.
example.english: He apologized to me.
example.fact: 道 carries several unrelated-seeming senses across common words — "road/way" in 道路, "to say" in 道歉 (literally "to speak an apology") and 知道 ("to know"), and "principle" in 道理 — a single character doing a lot of semantic work worth tracking across vocabulary rather than assuming one fixed meaning.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi xiàng tā dàoqiàn.
examples.english: You should apologize to her.

examples.hanzi: 我已经道歉了，可是她还在生气。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng dàoqiàn le, kěshì tā hái zài shēngqì.
examples.english: I've already apologized, but she is still angry.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings: 情 emotion, 快 happy, 怕 afraid; 怜 is feeling pity.
令 (lìng) is a loose sound hint (lián/líng); same part in 铃 líng and 零 líng.

example.hanzi: 这只小狗看起来很可怜。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī xiǎo gǒu kànqǐlai hěn kělián.
example.english: This little dog looks so pitiful.
example.fact: 可怜 can switch part of speech without changing form: as an adjective it means "pitiful" (他很可怜, "he's pitiful"), but placed before a person it becomes a verb meaning "to pity" (可怜可怜他, "have some pity on him") — the same two characters doing double grammatical duty.

examples.pinyin: Nà ge háizi zhēn kělián.
examples.english: That child is really pitiful.

examples.hanzi: 可怜的小鸟从树上掉下来了。
examples.pinyin: Kělián de xiǎo niǎo cóng shù shàng diào xiàlái le.
examples.english: The poor little bird fell from the tree.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地 earth, 坐 sit; 在 is "to be at a place".
才 (cái) is a close sound clue for zài; 才 also appears in 材 cái.

example.pinyin: Zhè dào tí shízài tài nán le.
example.english: This problem is really too hard.
example.fact: 实在 most often shows up as an intensifying adverb before an adjective ("really, truly" — 实在很难), a usage that has drifted quite far from its literal building blocks 实 ("real, solid") and 在 ("to exist, to be present") — "real and present" becoming, in effect, just "truly".

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shízài zǒu bu dòng le.
examples.english: I really can't walk any more.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ shízài bù zhīdào.
examples.english: I honestly don't know about this.
